newsitem.title: FRANCE: French airline flights near normal after strike.
newsitem.headline: French airline flights near normal after strike.

text.p: State-owned airline Air France Europe resumed flights out of Paris' Orly airport on Sunday as ground staff briefly kept up a two-day-old strike over airline restructuring plans, an airline spokeswoman said.
Air traffic was reported almost normal with only minimal delays despite the latest two-hour action by ground workers.

The strike over the regional airline's merger with parent company Air France forced cancellation of many flights on Friday and all flights on Saturday out of Orly, south of Paris, spoiling the Easter holiday weekend for many travellers.
A union spokesman disputed the airline's version and said management chose to cancel Saturday's flights although staff were not on strike.
Ground staff at Orly, Paris' second airport, voted to halt work for two hours from midday (1000 GMT) on Sunday, but the airline said flights were not being cancelled.
"We will continue to provide all flights," the Air France Europe spokeswoman said.
Ground workers are protesting against the unifying of their pay and employment terms with those of parent company Air France in a merger between the two airlines.
The airline said management would discuss union demands next week and delay until a disputed new working schedule May 1st.
Air France Europe pilots and flight crew have called a two-day strike over pay and conditions for next Monday and Tuesday but the company said all flights would take place.
